text: Howard Hughes built the biggest plane of its time out of wood. It flew once. For less than a minute.
In World War Two, metal was scarce, so the giant flying boat was made mostly of birch. Its wingspan was ninety-seven metres.
Critics called it the Spruce Goose. The Senate called Hughes in to explain the money.
In nineteen forty-seven, he lifted it twenty metres off the water, flew about a mile, and landed. It never flew again.
Dave is still waiting in the cockpit for the second flight.
